t.2.14.1: Having passed through the door of that inner palace, crowded with people, he who knew the ancient lore then reached a secluded chamber.
t.2.14.3: There at the door he saw the superintendents of the women's quarters stationed, aged men clad in ochre robes, staffs in hand, finely adorned and fully attentive.
t.2.14.2: The residence was guarded by young men bearing lances and bows, adorned with gleaming earrings, vigilant, single-minded and deeply devoted.
t.2.14.4: Seeing him approaching, they, eager to do what was pleasing to Rāma, quickly announced it to Rāma, who was with his wife.
t.2.14.5: Learning that the charioteer, his father's close confidant, had been announced, Rāghava, wishing to please his father, had him brought in right there.
t.2.14.6: The charioteer saw him, resembling Vaiśravaṇa, splendidly adorned and seated on a golden couch spread with a coverlet.
t.2.14.7: He saw the scorcher of foes anointed with costly sandal paste, pure and fragrant, that shone like the blood of a boar.
t.2.14.9: The bard, versed in proper observances, humbly saluted him, the bestower of boons, who blazed like the burning sun, endowed with his own splendor.
t.2.14.8: He was attended, moreover, by Sītā, who stood at his side with a yak-tail fan in her hand, like the moon joined with the star Citrā.
t.2.14.10: With joined palms, Sumantra, honored by the king, asked the prince whether he was at ease in his pastimes, his bed and his seat, and then spoke these words to him.
t.2.14.12: Thus addressed, the radiant lion among men was filled with joy. Then he honored Sītā and spoke these words.
t.2.14.11: Kausalyā is truly radiant, O lord! Your father, together with Queen Kaikeyī, wishes to see you; go there without delay.
t.2.14.13: O Devī, the king and the queen have met together and are surely consulting about some matter concerning my consecration, on my account.
t.2.14.14: For, having perceived his intention, the most gracious lady with intoxicating eyes, eager to do what is pleasing, is urging the king on my behalf.
t.2.14.15: As is the assembly gathered there, so is the messenger who has come; surely this very day the king will consecrate me as heir apparent.
t.2.14.16: Well then, going quickly from here, I shall see the lord of the earth; and you, together with your attendants, sit at ease and enjoy yourself.
t.2.14.17: Honored by her husband, dark-eyed Sītā followed her lord as far as the door, meditating on auspicious blessings for him.
t.2.14.18: Having seen all the petitioners, having met them and greeted them warmly, he then mounted the excellent chariot that blazed like fire.
t.2.14.20: Like thousand-eyed Indra mounting his swift chariot yoked with bay horses, Rāghava, blazing with splendor, mounted his chariot and set out quickly.
t.2.14.19: Gleaming like gold, as if stealing away the eyes with its radiance, and yoked with superb horses that were like young elephants.
t.2.14.21: Like a thundering rain-cloud in the sky, making all resound with his clamor, the glorious one went forth from his dwelling, as the moon emerges from a great cloud.
t.2.14.23: Then a tumultuous clamor of 'halahalā' arose on every side from that throng of people as it went forth.
t.2.14.22: Lakṣmaṇa, the younger brother of Rāghava, holding a parasol and a fly-whisk in his hands, mounted the chariot and, as a brother, guarded his brother from behind.
t.2.14.24: There Rāghava heard the chatter and talk of the assembled crowd, and the various words about himself spoken by the people in the city, who looked overjoyed.
t.2.14.25: Today this Rāghava goes to royal fortune through the king's favor, seeking its vast domain; we here, whose ruler he will be, have all our desires fulfilled. It is a gain for these people that he will obtain this whole kingdom for a long time.
t.2.14.27: Rāma beheld the splendid royal highway, crowded with female elephants, tuskers, chariots and horses, its crossroads filled with great throngs of people, abounding in jewels and heaped with many wares.
t.2.14.26: With noisy horses and elephants going before him, honored by heralds of blessings, bards and panegyrists, and praised by excellent musicians, he went forth like Vaiśravaṇa.
